question.text: A MASTER-FEEDER structure is used by the Sahyadri Stat-Arb Fund. Which statement BEST captures its mechanics?

answer.text: Offshore investors subscribe into a feeder fund in Mauritius/Singapore/GIFT-IFSC, which in turn invests into the domestic master AIF in India; management fees are charged at the master level and only a nominal fee at the feeder
Each investor gets a separate managed account which feeds into a pooled vehicle
All investors — onshore and offshore — must subscribe only through the feeder
The master fund invests in multiple feeder funds which hold the portfolio

explanation.text: The Logic: Master-feeder: offshore investors pool into a feeder (often Mauritius/Singapore/GIFT-IFSC), and the feeder invests its whole corpus into the master fund in India. The master fund also accepts direct investors (domestic/HNI/institutions). Management fee is usually charged at the master level; feeders charge only a nominal amount (e.g., USD 1,000 symbolic fee). The fee is passed to feeder investors via NAV allocation. The Trap: Option B describes managed accounts (not feeder). Option C is overstated — direct investors can invest in the master. Option D inverts the flow (master into feeders is wrong). Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C/D/A/B cover this taxonomy. GIFT-IFSC feeders are increasingly exam-relevant. Manager's Pro-Tip: For a Cat III manager, establishing a GIFT-IFSC feeder can route foreign capital without Mauritius/Singapore, while availing Section 80LA 100% tax holiday for 10 years on IFSC income — evaluate this for any new offshore raise.
